CRONOS is able to simulate the solar wind up through the Earth's orbit with a high degree of accuracy.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to produce realistic three-dimensional solar wind structures that are consistent with observations.
it is now possible to use a self-consistent MHD model for the entire heliosphere, starting with a detailed model of the solar surface and its magnetic field.
the CRONOS model, which has been successfully tested at the inner-heliosphere boundary, is now ready to be applied at the outer-heliosphere.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MHD simulation of the radial magnetic-field maps can reproduce the observed solar wind speed and density profiles at 1 AU, as well as the observed magnetic field strength, and that the solar wind at 1 AUs is not a superposition of the solar wind emanating at the equator and at the poles. [2]
the CRONOS code is capable of reproducing the solar wind structure and its evolution over the solar cycle.
the inner-heliosphere is not in a steady state and the magnetic field is highly variable, with the solar wind speed being the main driver of the evolution of the field.
